facts: These are three petitions under art. 32 by the petitioners, which is a partnership firm, praying for a declaration that s. 2 of the Madras General Sales Tax(Special Provisions) Act, 1963 (Act No. 11 of 1963)hereinafter called the Act, is ultra vires the Constitution and of no effect and for a writ of mandamus directing the State of Madras to refrain from enforcing any of the provisions of that section.

The petitioners are dealers in skin, carrying on business at Shenbakkam, Vellore, North Arcot District. in the State of Madras. They purchase raw skins from places both within and outside the State of Madras, tan the same and sell them through their agents in Madras.

They were assessed to a certain amount of sales-tax, in accordance with the provisions of the Madras General Sales Tax Act 1939 (Madras Act IX of 1939) and r.16(2)(ii) of the rules framed thereunder viz., the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, on the turnover of hides and skins purchased in the untanned condition outside the State, but tanned within the State, with respect to each of the assessment years 1955-56, 1956-57 and 1957-58.
The tax was assessed at 3 pies per rupee on the price of tanned hides and skins for the years 1955-56 and 1956-57 and at the rate of 2 per cent on the turnover for the year 1957-58.
Subsequently, the validity of r.16(1) of the rules was challenged in this Court in writ petitions Nos. 43 and 44 of 1963 by M. J. Jamal Mohideen & Co.
On June 10, 1963, the Governor of Madras promulgated Madras Ordinance No. 3 of 1963.
The relevant provisions of the Ordinance read: '2. Special provisions in respect of tax on sale of hides and skins in certain cases:-'

It is to be noticed that s. 2(1)of the Act is in respect of tax on sale of dressed hides and skins and not in respect of tax on sale of raw hides and skins with which clause (i) of s. 2(1) of the Ordinance dealt.
Consequently the other provisions of the other sub-sections of s. 2, though practically the same as those of the Ordinance, have been suitably modified.
issues: Is s. 2 of the Act ultra vires the Constitution?
Does s. 2(1) of the Act discriminate against imported untanned hides and skins?

Does s. 2(i) of the Act create discrimination between the case of a local merchant, selling locally dressed hides and skins and the case where the dealer who is the first seller in the State and who purchased only dressed hides and skins outside the State and then sold them in the State?
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners challenged earlier the validity of r. 16 on the ground that it contravened Art. 304 of the Constitution.
The petitioners argued that s. 2(1) of the Act discriminates against imported untanned hides and skins.

The petitioners argued that s. 2(i) of the Act creates discrimination between the case of a local merchant, selling locally dressed hides and skins and the case where the dealer who is the first seller in the State and who purchased only dressed hides and skins outside the State and then sold them in the State.
respondent_arguments: The Sales Tax Authorities negatived the petitioners' contentions.
The respondent argued that s. 2(1) of the Act does not discriminate against imported untanned hides and skins.

The respondent argued that s. 2(i) of the Act does not create discrimination between the case of a local merchant, selling locally dressed hides and skins and the case where the dealer who is the first seller in the State and who purchased only dressed hides and skins outside the State and then sold them in the State.
court_reasoning: The Court held that s. 2(1) of the Act discriminates against imported untanned hides and skins.

The Court held that s. 2(i) of the Act creates discrimination between the case of a local merchant, selling locally dressed hides and skins and the case where the dealer who is the first seller in the State and who purchased only dressed hides and skins outside the State and then sold them in the State.
holding: The Court declared that s. 2 of the Act is ultra vires the Constitution.
The Court granted a writ of mandamus directing the State of Madras to refrain from enforcing any of the provisions of s. 2 of the Act.
